text:
Eric Pohlkamp has been an NHL player for a week. The Sharks' fifth-round pick (132nd in 2023), a Minnesota kid who went from Bemidji State to the University of Denver, made his debut in Los Angeles on Nov. 4 and has played four games since, at about 16 minutes a night. He picked up his first NHL assist in Dallas and another in the shootout win over the Islanders, and San Jose Hockey Now wrote about the praise he's getting inside the team.

Four games tells us almost nothing, so here's what we do know. He scored 18 goals in 43 games for Denver last season, a lot for a college defenceman, worth roughly 30 points over 82 NHL games by our league translation. He's 5'11" and plays on the right side, paired with Dmitry Orlov in practice lines. The Sharks have been outplayed with him on the ice so far, about like the team overall. Our range on his season is very wide, from 12 to 36 points, which is the honest answer for a player this new. Watch his minutes over the next couple of weeks.
